newsitem.title: USA: Lili drifting, strengthening in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Lili drifting, strengthening in Caribbean.

text.p: Tropical Storm Lili drifted slowly in the Caribbean south of Cuba Wednesday, but was expected to resume its northward trek toward Cuba and Florida, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), Lili's center was near latitude 18.4 north and longitude 84.7 west or about 365 miles (585 km) south-southwest of Havana, Cuba.
The storm drifted to the west Wednesday and had taken up a slow northwest motion at about 7 mph (11 kph) by late afternoon, but was expected to turn toward the north Thursday, forecasters said.
Maximum sustained winds were near 65 mph (100 kph) in a small area near its center and some strengthening was likely during the next 24 hours.
Forecasters also warned that rainfall of 12 inches (30 cm) and higher was possible over parts of Cuba and Central America, which could produce flash floods and mudslides.

As of 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), a hurricane watch and tropical storm warning were in effect for the Isle of Youth and the western mainland provinces of Pinar Del Rio, Havana, Matanzas, Villa Clara and Cienfuegos in Cuba.
A tropical storm warning was in effect for the east coast of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula from Cabo Catoche south to Bahia de Chetumal and for the Cayman Islands.
